note: Expected differences between the web app's MIDI ledgers and the native MidiSched (owner's decision, 19 Nov 20:45: suspected web bugs are FIXED in the native port, the ledgers stay the web's truth). Each rule: case, B number, op, why, count. Ops: gear/stop (the web's message is expected shifted), drop (a web message native does not send), add (a native message the web does not send), move (a web message expected at another time), zone (clock ticks checked by the B2 rule). test_midi_ledger.cpp applies them and checks every count; an unlisted difference fails.

two tracks, one port + channel, the same pitch: the second track's retrigger sends an OFF first (web: a bare second ON)
the first track's OFF ends only its own hold: the other track still holds the pitch (web: one OFF ended both); the OFF goes out when the last holder lets go (1083, as the web)
a silent note (vol 00) ends the mono note that was sounding at its own time (web: at the next note, 125 ms later)
NEW (found while building): the web names a live key's column 'h' + (held keys + 1), so a key after a key-up gets the column of a key still held and ends it. Native keys have their own column
consequence: that key is still sounding at PANIC, which ends it (with the All Notes Off, as before)

ticks around the TPO 90 (120 -> 90 bpm): the web's ticks before the change are already at the new, slower spacing and irregular; native integrates the tempo map forward: regular 120 spacing until the change takes effect, then 90; monotonic, every interval between the two tick lengths
live tempo change 120 -> 140: same rule (web ticks bunch up before the change takes effect)
live tempo change 140 -> 97.5: same rule

companion to B9, found while building: the note that was sounding at the STOP lost its own OFF to the clear; the web leaves it to All Notes Off (CC 123), native sends the OFF for every note that really sounds, so a synth that ignores CC 123 does not hang
